content.prompt: A farmer needs to cross a river with a wolf, a goat and a cabbage. The boat carries the farmer and one more thing. The wolf can't be left alone with the goat, and the goat can't be left alone with the cabbage. What is the smallest number of crossings (counting trips there and back)?
hints: The goat is the problem: it can't stay with either of the other two.
Sometimes you need to bring something back to the starting bank.
content.explanation: Take the goat; go back alone; take the wolf; come back with the goat; take the cabbage; go back alone; take the goat: 7 crossings.

content.prompt: You have 9 identical coins, but one of them is slightly heavier. With a two-pan balance, what is the smallest number of weighings that guarantees finding the heavy coin?
hints: Each weighing has 3 possible results: left is heavier, right is heavier, or they balance.
Split the coins into 3 groups of 3.
content.explanation: Weigh 3 against 3: the heavy group (or the one left out) has the coin. Then weigh 1 against 1 from that group. 2 weighings are enough.

content.prompt: In a certain year, March 1 fell on a Monday. On what day of the week did April 1 fall that year?
hints: March has 31 days.
Every 7 days the day of the week repeats. What is the remainder of 31 ÷ 7?
content.explanation: 31 = 4 × 7 + 3: April 1 falls 3 weekdays after Monday, that is, Thursday.

content.prompt: Today, a father's age is three times his son's age. In 12 years, the father's age will be twice the son's age. How old is the son today?
hints: Call the son's age s. The father is 3s.
content.explanation: 3s + 12 = 2s + 24, so s = 12. The father is 36; in 12 years, 48 = 2 × 24.

content.prompt: In a dark drawer there are 10 black socks and 10 white socks, all loose. What is the smallest number of socks you must take out to be sure of getting a pair of the same color?
hints: Think about the worst case: total bad luck.
With 2 socks, you might get one of each color.
content.explanation: With 3 socks and only 2 colors, at least two are the same color (the pigeonhole principle).

content.prompt: In the same dark drawer, with 10 black socks and 10 white ones, what is the smallest number of socks you must take out to be sure of having a pair of BLACK socks?
hints: In the worst case, all the white ones come out first.
After the 10 white ones, how many black ones do you still need for a pair?
content.explanation: In the worst case the 10 white ones come out; then 2 more black ones: 10 + 2 = 12.

content.prompt: To number the pages of a book, from page 1 to page 120, how many digits are written in all?
hints: Separate the pages with 1 digit, 2 digits and 3 digits.
Pages 1 to 9: 9 digits. Pages 10 to 99: 90 pages with 2 digits each.

content.prompt: A snail is at the bottom of a 10-meter well. During the day it climbs 3 meters and at night it slides back 2 meters. On which day does it reach the top?
hints: At the end of each full day and night, it only moves up 1 meter.
Careful: on the day it reaches the top, it doesn't slide back anymore.
content.explanation: After 7 days and 7 nights it is at 7 m. On day 8 it climbs 3 m and reaches 10 m.

content.prompt: In a single-elimination tournament with 32 teams (whoever loses is out and there are no ties), how many games are played until there is a champion?
hints: Each game knocks out exactly one team.
How many teams need to be knocked out?
content.explanation: Every team except the champion is knocked out, one per game: 32 − 1 = 31 games.

content.prompt: How many squares, of all sizes, are there on a 3 × 3 board?
hints: Count the 1 × 1, 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 squares separately.
How many different positions can a 2 × 2 square take?
content.explanation: 9 squares of 1 × 1 + 4 squares of 2 × 2 + 1 square of 3 × 3 = 14.

content.prompt: Which letter continues the sequence: J, F, M, A, M, J, J, …?
hints: The letters don't follow the alphabet: think of something that has 12 parts.
J for January, F for February…
content.explanation: They are the first letters of the months: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August.

content.prompt: Three boxes are labeled "Apples", "Oranges" and "Mixed", but ALL the labels are wrong. You can take out a single fruit from one box, without looking inside. Which box should you take it from to work out what's in all of them?
hints: Since the "Mixed" label is wrong, that box has only one kind of fruit.
One fruit from that box reveals what it contains — and you can deduce the rest.
content.explanation: The "Mixed" box has only one kind of fruit. If you get an apple, it's the apple box; the "Oranges" box can't have oranges, so it has the mixed fruit, and the "Apples" box has the oranges.

content.prompt: A whole candle lasts 1 hour. From the leftovers of 3 burned candles, you can make 1 new candle. Starting with 9 candles, for how many hours at most can you have light?
hints: After burning the 9 candles, you have 9 leftovers.
The new candles leave leftovers too!
content.explanation: 9 candles (9 h) → 9 leftovers = 3 candles (3 h) → 3 leftovers = 1 candle (1 h). Total: 9 + 3 + 1 = 13 hours.

content.prompt: What is the smallest three-digit number, with all digits different, whose digits add up to 20?
hints: For the number to be small, the hundreds digit must be as small as possible.
The other two digits are at most 9 and 8 (different): they add up to at most 17.
content.explanation: With a hundreds digit of 1 or 2, the other two would have to add up to 19 or 18 without repeating — impossible. With 3: 8 + 9 = 17. The number is 389.

content.prompt: You have a 1 kg weight, a 3 kg weight and a 9 kg weight, and a two-pan balance. The weights can go on either pan. What is the largest whole weight (in kg) you can measure?
hints: Putting a weight on the same pan as the object is like subtracting it.
For example, 2 kg = 3 kg on one side and 1 kg next to the object.
content.explanation: The maximum is using all of them on the same side: 1 + 3 + 9 = 13 kg. And every value from 1 to 13 can be measured too.

content.prompt: A 200-meter train goes through a 400-meter tunnel at 20 meters per second. How many seconds pass from when the front of the train enters the tunnel until the back comes out?
hints: The front of the train has to travel the whole tunnel plus the length of the train itself.
Total distance ÷ speed = time.

content.prompt: At 2:30, what is the smaller angle, in degrees, between the hour hand and the minute hand?
hints: The minute hand is on the 6 (180°). The hour hand is not exactly on the 2!
The hour hand moves 30° per hour, that is, 0.5° per minute.
